To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current sustainable consumption policy framework is inadequate for dealing with the problems of environmental degradation in Asia-Pacific cities and that a ‘political ecology of consumption’ approach offers a more promising way forward for future research.

(i) consumption should become the central focus of future research on environmental issues in Asia- Pacific cities; (ii) consumption should not be viewed in isolation from the broader political and economic context; (iii) consumption should be understood in terms of the cultural values and practices that underpin it; and (iv) consumption should be viewed as a key site of political contestation and negotiation.
sustainable consumption is a promising policy framework for Asia-Pacific cities, although significant conceptual and practical difficulties exist.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to make consumption more sustainable, and to understand the social and cultural processes through which consumption occurs.
the ways in which consumption is implicated in the creation and reproduction of environmental problems in Asia-Pacific cities and the ways in which these problems might be addressed.
how the consumption of urban dwellers can be rethought to address current environmental problems.

sustainable consumption is a useful policy framework, but it should be used as a starting point to explore the political, economic and environmental issues of Asia-Pacific urban areas.
the political economy approach offers the most useful framework for understanding and addressing urban environmental problems in the region, especially in relation to consumption issues.
the current policy approach of sustainable consumption is not a panacea for Asia-Pacific cities.

the political ecology approach offers a way forward for research into Asia-Pacific cities, which will help us to understand the complex social, cultural and political dimensions of urban environmental issues.
consumption is a powerful force that shapes the environmental outcomes of Asia-Pacific cities, and therefore should form a key focus of urban environmental research.
consumption research is a promising avenue to explore urban environmental problems in Asia-Pacific cities.

the consumption of urban space is central to understanding current environmental problems.
consumption is a powerful tool for understanding the complex and often contested nature of environmental problems in Asia-Pacific cities.
consumption needs to be central to research into Asia-Pacific cities, as it reveals the complex and often contested ways in which environmental problems are constructed and addressed.
